Customs Guarantee Rules 2024: These rules are officially titled the Customs Guarantee Rules 2024.
The rules are set to come into force on the sixth day of June 2024, necessitated by the implementation of the Customs Act 2023.
Customs Act 2023: This is the primary legislation under which the Customs Guarantee Rules 2024 are enacted, establishing the legal requirement for the issuance of these rules.
The term Act is defined as the Customs Act 2023 for the purpose of these rules.
The rules establish that terms not specifically defined within this instrument shall carry the same meaning as provided in the Customs Act 2023.
Importer: The term Importer is defined by referencing the specific definition provided in the Customs Act 2023.
Exporter: The term Exporter is defined by referencing the specific definition provided in the Customs Act 2023.

processed_clauses.resolved_text: ৩। কাস্টমস গ্যারান্টির প্রযোজ্যতা।⎯ যে সকল ক্ষেত্রে এই আইন ও আইনের অধীন প্রণীত বিধি-বিধানে গ্যারান্টি গ্রহণের বিধান রাখা হইয়াছে কেবল সেই সকল ক্ষেত্রে কাস্টমস গ্যারান্টির ব্যবহার প্রযোজ্য হইবে।

Customs Guarantee: The use of a customs guarantee is strictly restricted to those instances where specific provisions for such guarantees have been made under the relevant customs law and its associated rules.
Customs Act 1969: The Act serves as the legal foundation for the applicability of customs guarantees, requiring that such mechanisms only be utilized when explicitly provided for within its own text or under rules derived from its authority.

তবে শর্ত থাকে যে, বোর্ড বিশেষ বিবেচনায় যৌক্তিক কারণ উল্লেখপূর্বক, কোনো নির্দিষ্ট পণ্য চালানের ক্ষেত্রে ব্যাংক গ্যারান্টি গ্রহণের পরিবর্তে অন্য কোনো কাস্টমস গ্যারান্টি গ্রহণের নির্দেশনা প্রদান করিতে পারিবে।

Customs Guarantee: The law requires the acceptance of unconditional and continuing bank guarantees for the provisional assessment and clearance of goods under specific legal provisions and Section 93 of the Customs Act 1969.
The National Board of Revenue holds the discretionary power to allow alternative forms of customs guarantees for specific consignments if justified by special circumstances and logical reasoning.
Customs Act 1969: This Act provides the foundational authority for requiring bank guarantees for the provisional clearance of goods under its various sections, including Section 93.
National Board of Revenue: The National Board of Revenue is authorized to permit the substitution of alternative customs guarantees in place of mandatory bank guarantees for specific consignments based on special consideration.

Customs Act 1969: Section 43 of this Act provides the legal basis for the acceptance of comprehensive guarantees for customs purposes.
Comprehensive Guarantee: This mechanism allows for the consolidated coverage of customs duties and charges, provided that the total value of the guarantee is not less than the cumulative duties and taxes payable on the goods.
It is applicable to Authorized Economic Operators, government entities, and organizations specified by the National Board of Revenue, as well as for transit and transshipment operations.
The instrument must be in the form of a bank guarantee when such a guarantee is otherwise required for the clearance of goods.
It is prohibited to use a comprehensive guarantee for operations, declarations, or customs procedures that involve two or more different types of guarantee requirements.
Authorized Economic Operator: These entities are explicitly eligible to utilize the comprehensive guarantee facility for their customs operations.
National Board of Revenue: The Board has the authority to specify which institutions, in addition to Authorized Economic Operators and government bodies, are permitted to provide comprehensive guarantees.
Transit and Transshipment: These operations are explicitly eligible for coverage under the comprehensive guarantee regime.

processed_clauses.resolved_text: ৬। গ্যারান্টি অবমুক্তকরণ।- বিধি ৪ বা আইনের আওতায় গ্রহণকৃত কাস্টমস গ্যারান্তিতে বিধৃত শর্তাদি পরিপালিত হইলে এবং প্রযোজ্য শুল্ক ও কর, চার্জ, ফি, ক্ষেত্রমত, সুদ ও জরিমানা, এবং অন্যান্য চার্জ নির্দিষ্ট মেয়াদের মধ্যে পরিশোধিত হইলে উক্ত কাস্টমস গ্যারান্টি অবমুক্ত করা যাইবে।

Customs Guarantee: A Customs Guarantee can be released once all conditions stipulated within it are fulfilled in accordance with the relevant rules or the Customs Act.
The release of the guarantee is further conditional upon the payment of all applicable customs duties, taxes, charges, fees, interest, and penalties within the specified timeframe.
Customs Act 1969: The Act serves as the legal framework providing the authority to accept and govern the conditions for the release of a Customs Guarantee.

Bank Guarantee: The document provides a standardized template for a bank guarantee, specifying that it must be unconditional and continuous in nature.
It serves as a legal instrument for importers or exporters to secure obligations towards the Customs authority.
Commissioner of Customs: The Commissioner of Customs is the designated beneficiary to whom the bank guarantee is submitted by the importer or exporter.
Business Identification Number: The template requires the Business Identification Number of the importer or exporter to be recorded for identification purposes within the guarantee document.
Bill of Lading: The template includes fields for transport documentation, such as the Bill of Lading, Air Waybill, or equivalent receipt, to link the bank guarantee to a specific shipment.

Business Identification Number: The Business Identification Number is required for importers and exporters when submitting customs declarations for the clearance of goods.
Commissioner of Customs: The Commissioner of Customs is the authority responsible for the assessment of duties, taxes, and other charges on imported or exported goods.
The Commissioner of Customs has the authority to permit the release of goods under an unconditional and continuous bank guarantee in lieu of immediate payment of customs revenue.
The Commissioner of Customs is empowered to demand encashment of a bank guarantee and initiate legal proceedings against the bank if the institution fails to honor the guarantee upon request.
Bank Guarantee: A bank guarantee serves as an unconditional and continuous financial security instrument submitted by a bank on behalf of an importer or exporter to facilitate customs clearance without immediate payment of duties and taxes.

The bank issuing the guarantee is contractually obligated to pay the specified customs revenue to the Commissioner of Customs upon demand without needing prior consultation with the importer or exporter.
Failure by a bank to encash a guarantee upon request by the customs authority makes the bank liable for legal action by the customs authorities.
